name: Curl Up and Die
label: Revelation
lede: Self-described nerds from Las Vegas, Curl Up and Die plugged into a generator to play the desert, got booed for asking moshers not to punch girls, and named a seven-minute song after a Carson Daly lookalike contest.

eras.title: Generators in the desert
eras.text: Las Vegas had almost nowhere for an all-ages metallic hardcore band to play. So Curl Up and Die played frat houses, a BMX crew's place, a racquetball court and the open desert, and learned to run.

years.h: A Vegas grindcore drummer becomes the singer
years.p: Mike Minnick, who'd drummed in Vegas grindcore band The Weirding Way, starts Curl Up and Die as its singer with guitarist Matt Fuchs and drummer Jesse Fitts. Demo tapes follow in 1998 and 1999.

years.cap: Flyer for a free all-ages show at The Batcave comic store, Las Vegas, May 16, 1999
years.h: No all-ages room in Vegas, so Curl Up and Die buy a generator
years.p: They play the desert off it. Guitarist Matt Fuchs remembers running across the sand with his amp, the police behind him.
years.xp:
The house shows weren't calmer. At a frat party the crowd expected pop-punk. In a West Side mansion the band set up in a racquetball court until the homeowner's father came down to confront them.

At one Halloween show the host's father body-slammed singer Mike Minnick, who was dressed as Tigger. Minnick says it seemed more playful than mean.

years.h: A Starship Troopers line becomes Curl Up and Die's first EP
years.p: The Only Good Bug Is a Dead Bug comes out on Status Records after a self-release. Guitarist Matt Fuchs later called the record sloppy and messy.

eras.title: A geek is a good thing
eras.text: Curl Up and Die called themselves weird, nerdy dudes in a scene that didn't reward it. Revelation signed them anyway, and Converge's guitarist recorded a debut full of sci-fi samples and very long song titles.

years.h: Status Records gathers the early tapes as 1998
years.p: Status Records puts Curl Up and Die's first recordings on one release titled 1998.

years.h: Booed in Las Vegas for asking moshers not to punch girls
years.p: Singer Mike Minnick told Vegas crowds it was fine to mosh but not to punch a girl in the face while she watched the show. People booed; guitarist Matt Fuchs is the one who remembers the ketchup.
years.xp:
Minnick says the Vegas scene splintered along subculture lines and a band of nerds didn't fit any of them.

At a bar-and-arcade venue a security guard maced the band's friends. Fuchs, whose guitar had been damaged, punched the guard. When the police sorted it out, the charges went against the guard.

q: A geek is a good thing.
yt: Live at the Grog Shop, Cleveland, Aug 5, 2002
years.h: Converge's guitarist records their Revelation debut
years.p: Unfortunately, We're Not Robots is made at God City Studio with [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]]. Sixteen tracks, some seconds long, two past seven minutes.
years.xp:
The long ones: You'd Be Cuter if I Shot You in the Face (8:10) and Rich Hall (Runner Up in a Carson Daly Lookalike Contest) (7:05). The lineup: Mike Minnick, Matt Fuchs, Ryan Hartery on bass, Jesse Fitts on drums. Revelation's first press was 311 on grey vinyl and 788 on black.

Minnick told Exclaim! the title is about wanting it easier: wanting to be a robot, with no feelings at all.
play: Rich Hall (Runner Up in a Carson Daly Lookalike Contest)

eras.title: The past isn't through with them
eras.text: Two EPs split one sentence between them, then a second album the band still calls its favorite, then a last show in Anaheim, the club they'd played more than any other outside Vegas.

years.h: One sentence, cut in half across two labels
years.p: We May Be Through with the Past... comes out on Status Records and But the Past Ain't Through with Us on Revelation. Read together, they finish each other.

years.h: A last album with Alex Newport behind the board
years.p: The One Above All, the End of All That Is is recorded at Hothead Studios with art by Dave Gorum. Mike Minnick and Matt Fuchs both call this era their favorite.
years.xp: Minnick told Punks in Vegas the last record is the one he likes most. Alex Newport produced it; Gorum, who drew the band's artwork, did the cover.

years.h: Curl Up and Die play their last show, at Chain Reaction in Anaheim
years.p: Chain Reaction is the club they'd played more than any other outside Las Vegas. Mike Minnick moves to Chicago, and Jesse Fitts has lost interest in metalcore.

eras.title: It always got hung up on a drummer
eras.text: Every reunion attempt stalled on the same problem: who plays drums. When Matt Fuchs's friend from junior high said yes, Curl Up and Die came back to the Anaheim room where they'd stopped.

years.h: Announced for Revelation's 25th, then pulled out
years.p: Revelation Records lists Curl Up and Die for its 25th anniversary shows before the band has sorted out travel. Distance, with Mike Minnick in Chicago, sinks it.
years.xp:
Minnick put it this way: "They announced us, and it was before we talked about how we would even get out there, money, all that."

Matt Fuchs said that back then a reunion just didn't seem as realistic.

years.cap: Mike Minnick leaning into the crowd, Chain Reaction, Anaheim, June 22, 2019
q: I don't play a show just to play a show.
years.h: The Chain Reaction reunion sells out
years.p: Fourteen years after their last show in the same Anaheim room, Curl Up and Die return with Keil Corcoran on drums, on a bill with Taken, Seizures and Regional Justice Center.
years.xp:
Mike Minnick expected little and got a show he called "far beyond anything I had anticipated." They played their longest set ever, from every era. Matt Fuchs's eyes were burning afterward, possibly from the rose water someone was spritzing.

The band's rule for the new lineup: members had to be friends first. Fuchs had known Corcoran since junior high.

years.cap: Poster for the Las Vegas homecoming show at the Bunkhouse Saloon, August 30, 2019
years.h: Curl Up and Die go home to the Bunkhouse Saloon
years.p: The Las Vegas date is billed as the homecoming. Matt Fuchs says the Bunkhouse sounds amazing, and the band joked about doing it in the desert instead, like the old days.

years.big: "Riff-wise, it covers everything from thrash to industrial."
years.h: A remote house in Joshua Tree is booked for new songs
years.p: Guitarist Matt Fuchs on the new material. Singer Mike Minnick says they'll keep pushing the electronic elements from the old records, fast and slow.
years.xp: The band plans writing sessions at a remote house in Joshua Tree. Minnick calls the new songs Curl Up and Die, just years later.
